subject.name: Company Reconnaissance
subject.name_mismatch: Directory says 'blog-worker', heir.yaml says 'Blog Worker', PROCESS.md says 'Company Reconnaissance'. The process evolved — downstream stages should flag this for alignment.

scope: Validate PROC-300 (Company Reconnaissance) against the executable-process invariant set from US run-003 (10 comparators across 24 layers) and Grid Reader structural requirements. This is a structuring validation run on an OPERATE-state process — checking whether the existing PROCESS.md satisfies all invariant layers, not building new content.
intent: Validate PROC-300 against unified template v6.0.0 and Grid Reader requirements. Operator wants to confirm the existing process document conforms to the invariant set discovered by US (10 comparators: L1 Executable Process, L5 Process Identity, L8 IMO Declaration, L9 Data Schema, L10 DMJ, L11 C&V, L12 Guard Rails, L13 Verification, L14 Measurement, L15 Execution Trace, L24 ORBT Gate Rules).

acceptance_criteria: All 10 invariant-set comparators evaluate to P=1 (pass)
IMO Declaration has Two-Question Intake answered + Middle table with 5 columns
OSAM has READ table, WRITE table, Join Chain to spine, Forbidden Paths
DMJ sections present: Define table, Map table, Join path
Guard Rails has >= 6 canonical stop conditions
Smoke Test has numbered steps with expected results + Three Primitives Check
Measurement has Process Metrics, Sigma Tracking, ORBT Gate Rules
Execution Trace has per-step entries with 14-field schema, append-only
ORBT Gate Rules has all 4 transitions defined with gate conditions
Grid Reader pattern: process is parseable as structured data, not prose

observations: PROC-300 is in OPERATE state with Run 1 complete (32,556 companies, 95.9% capture rate). This UP run is a structural validation, not a state change.
The PROCESS.md has 14 sections — maps well to the unified template's 3 clusters (Identity/Contract/Governance).
The heir.yaml exists but has naming inconsistency (Blog Worker vs Company Reconnaissance).
The PROCESS.md already contains math-engine comparators (C_1 through C_12) with tolerances and P(x;θ) — strong alignment with the mathematical principle.

DMJ sections (Define/Map/Join) are NOT explicitly labeled as such in the current PROCESS.md — the content may be present but not in the canonical DMJ table format. Downstream Define agent must evaluate.
Grid Reader requirement: the document is structured with tables and clear sections, but must be validated for machine-parseability at each layer.
